paragraph: [INACOM, Angola's communications regulator, reports 55.5% of individuals using the internet in 2024 (indicator HH8); no age range is given](<https://www.itu.int/itu-d/sites/projectumc/wp-content/uploads/sites/42/2025/11/Day-3-Angola.pdf>). The International Telecommunication Union's series [put the share at 34.6 per cent in 2021, 35.8 per cent in 2022, 37.9 per cent in 2023 and 40.7 per cent in 2024](<https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/dataportal>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 80 per cent or more has been found. Operating would need at least four in five people to use the internet.

In 2024, [8.6 per cent of the population](<https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/dataportal>) of Burundi used the internet, an estimate by the International Telecommunication Union. The same series [put the share at 6.8 per cent in 2021, 7.1 per cent in 2022 and 7.2 per cent in 2023](<https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/dataportal>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 25 per cent or more has been found, and no national survey or census figure for 2024 or later. Preparing would need at least a quarter of the population to use the internet.
